setting.formula: d\ge1,\quad V\in C^2(\mathbb R^d),\quad 0<\alpha I\preceq\nabla^2V(x)\preceq\beta I,\quad \kappa=\beta/\alpha,\quad \pi(dx)=Z^{-1}e^{-V(x)}dx
notes: The Hessian inequalities hold at every point; alpha and beta are positive real numbers. Separate Hessian-to-chord and Gibbs-integrability proofs support the compiled normalized PBPS augmentation certificate: positive Gibbs integral, probability and exact product-volume joint density. Consult linked cells for independent-review and admission states. Conditional kernels, the sampling process and its guarantees remain separate.
TV(P,Q) means sup over measurable events of |P(A)-Q(A)|. For probability laws with densities it is half their L1 distance.
R_2(P||Q)=log integral (dP/dQ)^2 dQ when P is absolutely continuous with respect to Q, and infinity otherwise. The PBPS paper writes D_2 and calls the target mu; here the common target is pi.
Expected oracle queries are not worst-case runtime. Reference-point preparation, proximal access and gradient-only reductions must be charged under the particular theorem's model.

cases.title: Smoothed Picard HMC and the proxy warm start
cases.role: Producer: low-accuracy transport control, then an implementable proxy warm start.

theorems.title: Low-accuracy W2 guarantee
theorems.anchor: SPHMC Theorem 1.1; Algorithm 3.2; Section 4.5; Appendix D
theorems.statement: Given a reference point with small gradient, the source algorithm outputs a probability law satisfying the displayed normalized Wasserstein error. This theorem counts gradient and proximal queries; gradient-only implementation is a separate reduction.
assumptions: The common C2 strong-convexity/smoothness setting.
0 < epsilon <= 1; a supplied x_ref satisfies ||grad V(x_ref)|| <= sqrt(alpha d).
Use the source algorithm and its parameter choices, not an arbitrary Picard or HMC discretization.

steps.title: Smooth the density
steps.formula: e^{-V_\eta}=e^{-V}*\mathcal N(0,\eta I),\qquad \nabla V_\eta(y)=\mathbb E[\nabla V(X)\mid X+\sqrt\eta G=y]
steps.text: This is not the Gaussian average of V. Differentiation under the integral and a specified conditional-law version justify the score identity. The implementable score estimator has bias as well as variance; it is not assumed exactly unbiased.

steps.title: Integrate the smoothed Hamiltonian equation
steps.text: Picard iteration approximates the trajectory, while Chebyshev–Lobatto quadrature approximates its integrals. Smoothing regularity, quadrature remainder and stochastic score error are separate inputs to the local-error estimate.

steps.title: Budget all three errors
steps.text: The first term includes iteration and numerical errors; the second is the smoothing bias. Finite second moments and the exact-kernel contraction must be supplied before using this triangle inequality.

theorems.boundary: No Wq, Renyi warmness, exact stationarity of a discretization, or cost-free proximal oracle follows from this W2 statement.

theorems.title: An implementable law near a Renyi-warm proxy
theorems.statement: For every allowed delta the algorithm produces the actual law below. A second, existential comparison law is close in TV and has bounded order-2 Renyi divergence. The comparison law need not be directly sampled.
assumptions: The common setting and the same reference-point bound as Theorem 1.1.
0 < delta < 1/2.
The recursive generator uses higher-moment smoothed sampling and terminal RGO implementation; this is not a general W2-to-Renyi implication.

steps.title: Turn a moment bound into a nearby bounded-displacement coupling
steps.text: For p >= 2 and finite p-moments, replace a coupled sample by its partner on the event where displacement exceeds r delta^(-1/p). Markov's inequality bounds that event; measurability and coupling attainment must be justified.

steps.title: Regularize both laws before measuring divergence
steps.text: A Gaussian reverse-transport bound applies after convolution. Recursive conditional/RGO updates then recover the desired unsmoothed target; deleting that recursion would change the theorem.

steps.title: Track the moving conditional target and oracle bill
steps.text: Completing the square closes the RGO family under another RGO. The recursive stages and outer proximal sampler improve conditioning; the kappa-squared setup term from Theorem 1.1 is not silently discarded.

theorems.boundary: Only the proxy has the displayed Renyi certificate. Genuine Renyi warmness of the actual output requires the stronger W_psi2 input in the separate source theorem.

cases.title: Picard HMC Part I: Gaussian cloud correction
cases.role: Recursive implementation route: turn Gaussian-cloud Picard updates into a finite sampler while keeping every adaptive call, cap event and replacement error auditable.

setting.formula: d\ge1,\quad V\in C^2(\mathbb R^d),\quad \|\nabla V(x)-\nabla V(y)\|\le\|x-y\|,\quad \pi(dx)=Z^{-1}e^{-V(x)}dx
notes: The source assumes the normalized target pi satisfies KL(mu||pi) <= (kappa/2) I(mu||pi) for every probability measure mu with smooth density, with kappa >= 1. This is an LSI assumption, not a pointwise strong-convexity hypothesis.
The supplied reference point satisfies ||grad V(x_ref)|| <= sqrt(d/kappa). No warm-start law is assumed.
The strongly log-concave specialization follows only after rescaling the smoothness and LSI constants; the general source theorem is stated under one-smoothness plus LSI.
Expected gradient queries include the paper's recursive Gaussian-cloud corrections, implemented RGO calls and cap/fallback accounting. They are not a worst-case runtime bound.

reader_guide: Start with the main theorem to see the accuracy and expected-query destination.
Read Lemma 6.1 to understand why the adaptive request forest has controlled size before the global cap.

bookkeeping.title: Section 6 recursive-call and accumulated-error ledger
bookkeeping.intro: The paper's adaptive sampler is easiest to audit as two coupled ledgers. The call ledger counts a breadth-first request forest. The error ledger compares ideal and implemented conditional kernels one slot at a time. They meet at the deterministic cap T_max; they must not be collapsed into one informal union bound.

theorems.title: Main high-accuracy sampling guarantee
theorems.statement: For the paper's sampler and parameter choices, a one-smooth target satisfying the displayed logarithmic Sobolev inequality can be sampled to total-variation error epsilon with the stated expected number of gradient queries, without a warm-start assumption.
assumptions: d >= 1; V is C2 on R^d and grad V is 1-Lipschitz; pi is the normalized law proportional to exp(-V).
pi satisfies KL(mu||pi) <= (kappa/2) times the relative Fisher information for every probability measure mu with smooth density, with kappa >= 1.
A supplied reference point x_ref satisfies ||grad V(x_ref)|| <= sqrt(d/kappa).
0 < epsilon <= 1/4; use the source Gaussian-cloud sampler, proximal wrapper and exact parameter schedule rather than an arbitrary Picard discretization.

steps.title: Represent dependent Picard evaluations by Gaussian clouds
steps.text: The cloud representation exposes independent Gaussian blocks while preserving the shared dependence needed by Picard iteration. Fluctuation and mean corrections are separate FORS gadgets; independence may not be invented between recursively shared blocks.

steps.title: Assemble a finite adaptive computation
steps.text: Mandatory predecessor chains are contracted into vertices and optional nested requests become children. Lemmas 6.1 and 6.2 control vertices and attached RGO queries before the deterministic global cap is imposed.

steps.title: Telescope every implementation error
steps.text: Dummy filling converts early termination into a common fixed slot space. Hybrids replace one conditional kernel at a time under the ideal history; the cap failure is added only after comparing capped and uncapped ideal algorithms.

steps.title: Insert the Section 6 budgets into the cloud sampler
steps.text: Theorem 6.4 fixes h, smoothing levels, Picard depth, phase count, local correction budgets and RGO accuracies. The proximal wrapper then restores general condition number kappa and produces Theorem 1.1.

theorems.boundary: No local Lean theorem yet proves the sampler, the adaptive forest, or the complexity bound. The big-O hides only universal constants specified by the source parameter choices; it is not a license to omit kappa, dimension, precision, cap or initialization dependencies.

theorems.title: Size and query count of a capped adaptive tree
theorems.statement: A breadth-first request queue with conditionally sub-Poisson child counts and mean offspring at most one quarter has expected total size at most four thirds of its root count and a subexponential upper tail. A deterministic local query cap multiplies the vertex bound.
assumptions: q >= 1 roots; A_0=q and, while A_v>0, A_{v+1}=A_v-1+zeta_{v+1} with zeta_{v+1} a nonnegative integer adapted to the exploration filtration.
Deterministic m >= 1 and lambda >= 0 satisfy E[exp(s zeta_{v+1}) | F_v] <= exp(lambda(exp(ms)-1)) on {A_v>0}, for every 0 <= s <= 1/m.
m lambda <= 1/4; T is the first v with A_v=0. The local reference-query count per processed vertex is at most Q_loc.
theorems.formula: \mathbb ET\le\frac{4q}{3},\qquad \mathbb P\{T>C(q+mu)\}\le e^{-u}\ (u\ge1),\qquad Q_{\rm ref}\le Q_{\rm loc}T

steps.title: Differentiate the conditional MGF at zero
steps.text: This supplies negative queue drift while the process is alive. Lean must state the conditional-expectation version and the stopped extension after the queue empties.

steps.title: Sum the stopped drift
steps.formula: \mathbb E A_{n\wedge T}\le q-\tfrac34\,\mathbb E(n\wedge T)
steps.text: Nonnegativity of the queue yields a uniform bound on the stopped exploration time; monotone convergence then gives the expectation bound for T.

steps.title: Build the exponential supermartingale
steps.text: The conditional MGF assumption controls the stopped queue and gives the tail with a universal constant C. This step must track the permitted range 0 <= s <= 1/m rather than optimize over an illegal exponent.

theorems.boundary: This lemma counts a dominating potential request tree. It does not prove that any particular FORS/cloud implementation satisfies the MGF premise, and it does not include RGO-internal query counts except through the separate attachment analysis.

theorems.title: Adaptive conditional-kernel TV error telescope
theorems.statement: For ideal and implemented adaptive algorithms stopped at the same deterministic number of slots, the output-law error is at most the sum of the mean conditional replacement errors evaluated along the ideal capped histories, plus the probability that the uncapped ideal algorithm exceeds the cap.
assumptions: For each slot 1 <= t <= T_max, K_t(H,.) and Khat_t(H,.) are measurable probability kernels on a common history/output interface.
Both capped algorithms use the same deterministic T_max and append a measurable dummy symbol after termination.
The uncapped ideal algorithm exceeds T_max with probability at most epsilon_cap.
H_{t-1} is the ideal capped history and delta_t is the expectation of TV(K_t(H_{t-1},.), Khat_t(H_{t-1},.)).

steps.title: Freeze a common finite history space
steps.text: Dummy filling makes every adaptive run a fixed-length record. This is what permits the t-th conditional rule to be compared without pretending that both algorithms made the same random number of calls.

steps.title: Define adjacent hybrids
steps.text: Consecutive hybrids share the ideal history distribution through slot t-1. Therefore the only new discrepancy is the conditional kernel at slot t, averaged under precisely that ideal history.

steps.title: Use data processing for the adaptive suffix
steps.text: All later calls may depend on the replaced output, but they form one common measurable downstream kernel for this adjacent pair. Data processing absorbs that adaptive continuation.
steps.support_note: The reusable mean conditional-error and common-suffix edges compile. Constructing the paper's dummy-filled history and identifying its slot law remain open.

steps.title: Telescope the capped adjacent hybrids
steps.text: Apply the triangle inequality to the fixed finite list of hybrid event probabilities. Every slot budget is charged once with unit coefficient.
steps.support_note: The finite real telescope compiles. Its application still needs the source-specific hybrid laws and adjacent bounds.

steps.title: Add cap failure once
steps.text: A final coupling or event comparison handles ideal capped versus ideal uncapped output. This is a separate proof edge, so the cap term is not repeated at every slot.

theorems.boundary: The mean conditional-event integral, common-suffix contraction and finite real telescope now compile as reusable Lean edges. The exact dummy-filled history kernel, source-specific delta_t identification and measurability, and capped/uncapped comparison remain separate red obligations; therefore Lemma 6.3 itself is not yet formalized. Uniform epsilon is only a corollary after those adapters.

cases.title: Proximal BPS: high accuracy from a warm start
cases.role: Consumer: a Renyi-warm input becomes a high-accuracy position law through an augmented-state discrete chain.

theorems.title: Optimized expected gradient complexity
theorems.statement: With universal positive tuning constants, run the implementable algorithm with the source parameter choices. Its output is epsilon-close to the target in TV and has the following expected gradient-query bound. No fixed worst-case running-time claim is made.
assumptions: The common setting; an input probability law mu_0 with R_2(mu_0||pi) <= Delta, where Delta >= 1.
0 < epsilon < 1/4; query access to grad V and a sample from mu_0.
Choose L and eta below and the iteration, resampling, error and solver budgets in source (4.8)–(4.9). The constants c_opt and K_opt are universal, not arbitrary user choices.
theorems.formula: \begin{gathered}L=\Delta+\log\frac{K_{\rm opt}d\kappa}{\varepsilon},\quad\eta=\frac{c_{\rm opt}}{\beta(\sqrt{dL}+L)},\quad\operatorname{TV}(\mathcal L(\widehat X),\pi)\le\varepsilon,\\\mathbb E Q_\nabla\le K_{\rm opt}\sqrt\kappa(d+L)^{1/4}L^{3/4}\left(\Delta+\log\frac4\varepsilon\right)\log(\kappa L).\end{gathered}

steps.title: Augment, then reflect the auxiliary variable
steps.text: Gaussian symmetry preserves the augmented law under this reflection. It differs from velocity reflection at a bounce. A conditional half-turn and occasional RGO resampling form the ideal transition; they are not independent ordinary Gibbs redraws at every step.

steps.title: Use discrete hypocoercivity, not a reversible gap shortcut
steps.formula: f=\mathbb E[f\mid Y]+(f-\mathbb E[f\mid Y]),\qquad\chi^2(\nu_0\mathcal K^{JN}\Vert\pi_\eta)\le e^{-J}\chi^2(\nu_0\Vert\pi_\eta)
steps.text: The source chooses eta, rho and a block length N as in Theorem 3.5. Conditional resampling damps the fluctuation; reflection couples it to the conditional mean. A modified L2 energy and half-turn operator bounds are essential. The local unrefreshed process alone need not mix.

steps.title: Keep implementation mismatch separate from ideal mixing
steps.text: Solver failure, approximate RGO draws and capped bounce rates each consume an error budget a. Lifted Renyi control bounds bad events along the ideal chain; a coupling union bound transfers its convergence to the implemented output.

steps.title: Balance localization against block length
steps.text: Substitute the chosen eta into the iteration bound and charge proximal solves, RGO calls and candidate bounce queries. Retaining L prevents a hidden warmness or precision dependence from disappearing into the dimension exponent.

theorems.boundary: This is the discrete augmented Proximal BPS algorithm with curved conditional flights. It is not vanilla continuous-time BPS, and its acceleration does not follow just from invariance or an algebraic reflection identity.

theorems.title: Stationary and finite-iteration lower bounds: source Theorem1.2 (informal)
theorems.statement: For each Table1 method and every sufficiently small normalized step h, there is a strongly convex smooth target of bounded condition number and a position initialization with expected potential gap at most C*d. For every sufficiently small epsilon, attaining sqrt(alpha)W2(position law after N steps,pi)<=epsilon requires the Table1 lower-bound number of queries up to logarithms. For underdamped methods the initial momentum is independent standard Gaussian. This is the source-labelled informal overview; stationary bias and finite-iteration claims keep their separate precise source contracts.

steps.text: Oscillatory targets yield the deterministic Heun obstruction; Gaussian/anisotropic Gaussian targets give exponential-midpoint bounds. Stationary bias alone does not establish every finite-step initialization claim.

steps.text: For the actual randomized methods, shared quadrature choices induce common covariance fluctuations. The source Section6 calculations and finite-step passage must be formalized under their actual randomness; independent coordinates must not be invented unconditionally.

composition.title: Cold start to high accuracy: the producer–consumer contract
composition.role: Composition view of SPHMC Theorem 1.3, not a third paper or an ASTIS novelty claim.

theorems.title: Compose through a proxy, with an explicit TV budget
theorems.anchor: SPHMC Theorem 1.3 and its proof in Section 7.2; PBPS Theorem 4.3 / Corollary 4.4
theorems.statement: Given the supplied small-gradient reference point, warm-start generation followed by Proximal BPS yields the stated TV accuracy and expected gradient cost. Algorithmic order is HighAccuracyEngine after WarmStartGenerator.
assumptions: The common setting; ||grad V(x_ref)|| <= sqrt(alpha d); 0 < epsilon < 1/4.
Use one measurable implemented probability kernel K for both the actual input law and its comparison law.

The PBPS input certificate uses the same normalized target, order-2 Renyi convention and gradient oracle. Its source warmness bound is Delta, not Delta squared; SPHMC Theorem 7.2 reparameterizes that symbol.

steps.title: Produce the implementable law and retain its witness
steps.text: The stronger Theorem 7.1(ii), with its accuracy parameter set to 1/2, supplies this witness. We run the next algorithm on mu, not on the existential mu-dagger.

steps.title: Apply TV data processing to the same implemented kernel
steps.text: For a measurable event A, the probability-kernel function x ↦ K(x,A) lies in [0,1]. The layer-cake identity writes its integral against the difference of the two probability laws as an integral of event differences, each bounded by TV. Taking the supremum over A proves the inequality without assuming a density for mu.
steps.anchor: SPHMC Section 7.2; ASTIS expansion of the data-processing step

steps.title: Use the warm theorem only on the witness
steps.text: The witness satisfies the warm hypothesis with budget 1. The kernel's warm-start error is epsilon/2; the triangle inequality adds, rather than multiplies, the two errors.

steps.title: Transfer accuracy and cost by different arguments
steps.formula: \mathbb E(Q_{\rm warm}+Q_{\rm engine})=\mathbb E Q_{\rm warm}+\mathbb E Q_{\rm engine}
steps.text: TV proximity alone cannot bound an unbounded query count. PBPS uses a fixed iteration budget, capped proximal solves, bounded candidate-event intensity and uniformly controlled expected RGO queries after a residual check. Port the conditional cost bound for the actual input before using linearity of expectation; do not borrow only the proxy's expected cost.
steps.anchor: PBPS Algorithm 2 and (4.18); SPHMC (7.1) and Section 7.2

theorems.boundary: The source theorem is known; every new local formal edge here remains red. Neither a generic Wasserstein-to-Renyi conversion nor a certified category/functor is claimed.

technologies.title: Density smoothing and score regularity
technologies.target: Normalized convolution, conditional score/covariance representatives and controlled higher derivatives.
technologies.boundary: Not potential averaging; not an exactly unbiased score oracle.

technologies.title: Picard trajectory and quadrature error
technologies.target: Integral Hamiltonian flow, local bias/variance and Wp propagation with finite moments.
technologies.boundary: Higher derivatives of the smoothed density do not strengthen assumptions on the original potential for free; oracle bias must be paid.

technologies.title: Truncation and reverse transport
technologies.target: A probability-law witness with separate TV distance and Renyi certificate, using p-moment and heat-flow inputs.
technologies.boundary: An actual sample law is not its comparison witness; smoothing and recursion cannot be removed.

technologies.title: Quadratic RGO composition
technologies.target: Complete the square once; keep potential equality up to a constant separate from equality of normalized conditional kernels.
technologies.boundary: Positive variance, normalization and parameter measurability are real obligations.

technologies.title: Two reflections with different roles
technologies.target: Velocity reflection R_h with R_0=I; separately the augmented involution (x,y) ↦ (x,2x-y).
